inline_comments.comment: `useHtmlLabels` is being passed as the `addBackground` parameter (5th argument) to `createLabel`. The `addBackground` parameter controls whether to apply the `labelBkg` CSS class to the label container, but `useHtmlLabels` is a boolean indicating whether the HTML label rendering path is active — a completely different concept. Since HTML labels are enabled by default, this will unconditionally add the background class to all four edge terminal labels (`startLabelLeft`, `startLabelRight`, `endLabelLeft`, `endLabelRight`) for the vast majority of users, causing unintended background styling on edge labels. The same mistake appears at lines 120, 143, and 167. These calls should pass `false` (or an explicit `edge.addBackground` if edge labels are ever meant to have a background), not `useHtmlLabels`.

This line was changed from `evaluate(getConfig()?.htmlLabels)` to `evaluate(getConfig()?.flowchart?.htmlLabels)`. This bypasses the canonical `getEffectiveHtmlLabels()` helper in `config.ts`, which (a) prefers the top-level `config.htmlLabels` over the deprecated `config.flowchart.htmlLabels`, and (b) issues the `FLOWCHART_HTML_LABELS_DEPRECATED` warning when the old location is used. By accessing `flowchart?.htmlLabels` directly, nodes rendered through `labelHelper` will silently ignore a user's top-level `htmlLabels: true` setting and only honour the deprecated nested path. Replace with `evaluate(getEffectiveHtmlLabels(getConfig()))` to stay consistent with how every other caller determines HTML label mode.

`createLabel` is an `async` function, so this call returns a `Promise`, not a DOM element. `elem.node().appendChild(label)` will append the Promise object rather than a node, and `label.getBBox()` will throw a `TypeError`. This function needs to be made `async` and the call needs `await`. This was a pre-existing bug, but the PR modified this line (adding `false, node.width`) without correcting it, so it remains broken.

`style.replace('color:', 'fill:')` will throw a `TypeError` if `style` is `null` or `undefined`. Notice that the HTML-label path directly above (line 104) already guards against this with a ternary: `style ? style.replace('fill:', 'color:') : style`. The same guard is missing here for the SVG text path. Callers such as `rectWithTitle.ts` pass `node.labelStyle` which can be `undefined`. Add the same guard: `style ? style.replace('color:', 'fill:') : ''`.

Same unchecked `.replace()` on `style` as in `dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js` line 109. If `style` is `undefined`, this will throw. The HTML-label path on line 108 of this file already guards with a ternary. Apply the same null check here.

`log.debug` was changed to `log.info` here. Project guidelines specify using `log.debug()` or `log.trace()` for development tracing inside rendering utilities, not `log.info()`. This line should be reverted to `log.debug('vertexText' + vertexText)` — or removed entirely before merging if it is not expected to survive in production.

`getConfig()` is called twice in the ternary: once for the truthiness check on line 34 and again to read the value on line 35. Each call traverses and merges config state. Cache the result in a local variable before the ternary: `const config = getConfig(); const bodyFontSize = config.fontSize ? config.fontSize : window.getComputedStyle(document.body).fontSize;`

The previous implementation had `div.style('padding-right', '1px')` which has been silently removed. While the intent may be to align with `createText`, this is a visible style change for all existing callers (cluster titles, `rectWithTitle`, edge labels, etc.). If the removal is intentional, the PR description should explain why the padding is no longer needed and any visual regression testing should confirm no layout shifts.

The changeset is marked `patch` with the message "no markdown-specific changes", but the PR actually enables KaTeX rendering (`hasKatex` / `renderKatexSanitized`) and text wrapping in `addHtmlLabel` — features that were not available through `createLabel` before. Per project rules, changesets that add features should be `minor`. The description is also inaccurate: KaTeX is a math/markdown rendering feature. Consider updating both the semver level and the description to accurately reflect the new capabilities.

general_comments.comment: The PR's stated goal is to reduce duplication by making `createLabel` a thin wrapper, but the diff introduces *more* duplication. `dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js` and `rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js` now contain near-identical copies of `addHtmlLabel`, `getWrappingWidth`, and `DEFAULT_WRAPPING_WIDTH = 200`. Any future change to the label rendering logic (e.g., a layout tweak or a KaTeX fix) will need to be applied in both files. Consider extracting the shared `addHtmlLabel` implementation into a single location (e.g., a new `rendering-util/rendering-elements/htmlLabel.js`) and importing it in both `createLabel` files, or — since both files are already marked `@deprecated` in favour of `createText` — evaluate whether one of them can simply re-export the other.

In both `addHtmlLabel` implementations (`dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js` and `rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js`), a hidden `tempSvg` element is appended to `document.body` for measurement and then removed at the end. If `configureLabelImages` throws (e.g., a rejected Promise inside), execution never reaches `tempSvg.remove()`, permanently leaking the hidden SVG into the DOM. Wrap the measurement block in a `try/finally` to guarantee cleanup: `try { await configureLabelImages(...); ... fo.attr(...); } finally { tempSvg.remove(); }`.
